definitions.short: Beor , the name of the father of an Edomitish king; also of that of Balaam
definitions.full: H1160. Beor בְּעוֺר proper name, masculine ( a burning ; ᵑ7 torch ) — 1 father of Balaam Num 22:5 ; 31:8 ; Deut 23:5 ; Josh 13:22 ; 24:9 ; Micah 6:5 ; בְּעֹר Num 24:3 , 15 ( ב ׳בנו ). 2 father of בֶּלַע , a king of Edom Gen 36:32 = 1Chr 1:43 .
definitions.rootNote: from 1197 (in the sense of burning); a lamp ;

occurrences.englishText: Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.

He sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, to Pethor, which is by the River, to the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, “Behold, there is a people who came out of Egypt. Behold, they cover the surface of the earth, and they are staying opposite me.
He took up his parable, and said,
He took up his parable, and said,
They killed the kings of Midian with the rest of their slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam the son of Beor with the sword.
Nevertheless Yahweh your God wouldn’t listen to Balaam, but Yahweh your God turned the curse into a blessing to you, because Yahweh your God loved you.
The children of Israel also killed Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, with the sword, among the rest of their slain.
Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse you,
Now these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel: Bela the son of Beor; and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
